experiments.question: Can annotated values preserve ABI and avoid default-path/per-item overhead?
alternatives: Existing XdmValue reference-slot annotated payload, with reference-backed accessors audited
controls: Positive and foreign provenance; array/map retention
Old public accessors and exact unchanged default-path behavior
measure: Allocation, boxing, accessor throughput and retained metadata
Small and large collections; precomputed data outside timed loops
experiments.decision: Choose neither until layout/default-path equivalence and required type access succeed; compare real workload budgets

experiments.question: Where do provenance and list/union distinctions survive or disappear?
alternatives: Internal carrier propagation across ordinary VM values
Explicit boundary wrapper with audited conversions
controls: Atomic/list/union including empty and singleton list
Atomization, casts, numeric operations, comparisons/hash and map keys
No typed value, nilled empty value, foreign components and serializer refusal
measure: Expected origin/type/list-boundary observations at every transition
experiments.decision: Record explicit preservation/strip/refusal laws against immutable adoption before semantic implementation; a lost required boundary rejects the design

experiments.question: Does authority API granularity impose repeated lookup or eager closure costs?
alternatives: Scalar authority operations plus immutable-array bulk closure
controls: Small/large component graphs, cycles and repeated queries
Foreign handle and unsupported closure must refuse completely
No name/digest authority cache; warm/cold cache separated
measure: Dispatch/provider crossings, allocations, closure memory and latency
experiments.decision: Select batch/cursor additions only if actual owner workloads justify them; never truncate to fit budgets

experiments.question: Can host operation admission retain actual resources through deferred work and worker failure?
alternatives: Explicit host-owned lifetime and optional admission lease
Chosen Braid worker-owned reopen or approved broker; separate controlled in-process profile
controls: Entry/closing race, reentry/callback close and blocked work
Nested/deferred access, cached Current and copied scalar after close
Caller cancellation versus raw completion, fault, timeout/child kill
Actual owned snapshot/generation/reader leases, no live-authority serialization
measure: Dispatch/release event order and exactly-once accounting
Latency to first item/cancellation/drain and actual resource observations
Unchanged source/store bytes and retained artifact identity
experiments.decision: No release on canceled wait alone; no universal disposal or concurrency claim. Scope lifecycle/protocol signatures from actual supported schedules
